Let \(L=f(r)^2\dot\theta\) be the Clairaut constant of a unit-speed geodesic. At the boundary \(f(R)=1\), the tangential speed is \(\sin(\arcsin c)=c\), so \(L=c\). Hence
\[
\dot r^2+f(r)^2\dot\theta^2=1,\qquad f(r)^2\dot\theta=c,
\]
and along one half of the geodesic, from its turning point \(f=c\) to the boundary \(f=1\),
\[
\Phi(c)=\int_{f=c}^{1}\frac{c}{x\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}\frac{dr}{dx}\,dx.
\]
Write
\[
q(x)=\frac{dr}{df}\bigg|_{f=x}.
\]
Then
\[
\Phi(c)=\int_c^1 \frac{c\,q(x)}{x\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}\,dx.
\]

For \(q(x)=1\),
\[
\int_c^1 \frac{c}{x\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}\,dx=\arccos c.
\]
So the extra term must come from \(q(x)-1\). We claim
\[
q(x)=1+\lambda x^2.
\]
Indeed,
\[
\int_c^1 \frac{c\,x^2}{x\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}\,dx
=c\int_c^1 \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}}\,dx
=c\sqrt{1-c^2}.
\]
Thus
\[
\Phi(c)=\arccos c+\lambda c\sqrt{1-c^2}
\]
is exactly equivalent to
\[
\frac{dr}{df}=1+\lambda f^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
r=f+\frac{\lambda}{3}f^3,\qquad R=1+\frac{\lambda}{3}.
\]

Now suppose the metric is induced by
\[
X(r,\theta)=(f(r)\cos\theta,f(r)\sin\theta,z(r)).
\]
Since \(r\) is meridian arclength,
\[
f'(r)^2+z'(r)^2=1.
\]
But
\[
f'(r)=\frac1{1+\lambda f(r)^2}.
\]
So a real \(z'(r)\) exists iff
\[
\frac1{(1+\lambda f^2)^2}\le 1
\]
for all \(0\le f\le1\). Since \(\lambda\neq0\), this holds exactly when
\[
\lambda>0.
\]
For \(-1<\lambda<0\), one has \(1+\lambda f^2<1\) for \(f>0\), so \(f'(r)>1\), impossible for a Euclidean surface of revolution parametrized by arclength.

For \(\lambda>0\),
\[
z'(r)=\sqrt{1-\frac1{(1+\lambda f^2)^2}},
\]
and therefore
\[
H=z(R)=\int_0^R z'(r)\,dr
=\int_0^1 \sqrt{(1+\lambda f^2)^2-1}\,df.
\]
Thus
\[
H=\int_0^1 f\sqrt{\lambda(2+\lambda f^2)}\,df
=\sqrt{\lambda}\int_0^1 f\sqrt{2+\lambda f^2}\,df.
\]
Using \(u=2+\lambda f^2\), \(du=2\lambda f\,df\),
\[
H=\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{2\lambda}\int_2^{2+\lambda}u^{1/2}\,du
=\frac{(2+\lambda)^{3/2}-2^{3/2}}{3\sqrt{\lambda}}.
\]

Hence the realizable pairs are exactly
\[
\boxed{\left\{\,\left(\lambda,\frac{(2+\lambda)^{3/2}-2^{3/2}}{3\sqrt{\lambda}}\right):\lambda>0\,\right\}.}
\]
